_meta.v2Note: Adds movement.dowseBudgetMilli (world-stage W30). A dowser sees four lanes out (Prospecting.DowserSightLanes) against a scout's two, so it costs more of the march than Scout's own 500 (half a turn) -- 250 (a quarter) is a starting value, not a measured one: it is the number a balance pass moves first.
_meta.v3Note: Adds growth and seasons (world-map W42, spec-sector-development.md). Schema-only: every growth pulse/multiplier ships at its identity value (seatPulsePerWeek 0, both multipliers 1000-per-mille) and every season multiplier ships at 1000-per-mille, so nothing downstream moves a hash -- W43-W49 wire the mechanism against these identity numbers, and W58 is the single later publish that turns them on (TurnEngine.RulesetVersion 5 -> 6, ask-first per the spec's own boundaries). growth.legionTarget is the one exception: it is the real, already-decided calibration target (world-stage-ideal.md SS8e.3), read only by the acceptance harness (W59), never by the engine -- a legion count the engine enforced would be a hard progression ceiling (AGENTS.md). raiseCostPoints and seasons.count/monthsPerSeason are provisional placeholders in the LoamPolicy sense (LoamPolicy.cs:5-9): they give the harness something to run against; picking them well is the harness's job, not this task's.
_meta.v4Note: Adds growth.raiseMemberHp (world-map W51, spec-sector-development.md SS1). A raised legion is one Fighter member at level 1; its species comes from the sector's climate (CreatureSpeciesCatalog.ElementPrimary, filtered zombie-side, picked deterministically by SpeciesId), never a new selection mechanism. 110 matches the shipped templates' own per-member Hp (WorldTemplateCatalog.cs) -- a provisional placeholder in the same LoamPolicy sense as raiseCostPoints, not a harness-tuned number. This is a schema-only addition: RecruitStock stays 0 in every shipped scenario until W58 turns growth on, so no `raise` order can ever afford to resolve today and this value moves no golden.
_meta.rebalanceLabel: W58: turn on real growth pulse (lair-heavy burst) and season upkeep cadence
_meta.v5Note: world-map W58 (spec-sector-development.md SS1/SS2, TurnEngine.RulesetVersion 6 -> 7, decisions.md): turns the growth pulse and the season upkeep term on for real. `growth.seatPulsePerWeek` 0 -> 20 (a modest per-seat trickle -- five Seats in `first-light`, 5-6 week boundaries in a 40-turn run, so a bare seat alone contributes only ~100-120 points, well under `raiseCostPoints`(100) x `growth.legionTarget`'s 6-10 floor by itself); `growth.lairMultiplierMilli` 1000 -> 4000 and `growth.specialWeekMultiplierMilli` 1000 -> 1500 (the lair-heavy-burst decision: a cleared lair quadruples its sector's pulse, a special week adds half again on top -- `first-light` has exactly one lair, at ember-hollow, so holding it is what turns a slow trickle into a real rate, not a second seat). `seasons.upkeepMilli` [1000,1000,1000,1000] -> [1000,850,1100,1400] -- season 0 stays identity on purpose (any fixture defaulting `CurrentTurn` to 0 sees no change), season 1 is favourable (-15%), seasons 2/3 progressively harsher (+10%/+40%), a real, legible cycle rather than four copies of 1000. `seasons.monthsPerSeason` 3 -> 1 (28-day seasons, not 84) so a season boundary (turn 28) falls inside W59's own forty-turn acceptance window -- at monthsPerSeason 3 no boundary could ever be observed in 40 turns, which would have made W59's own stated acceptance ('a season boundary is observable inside the forty turns') impossible to satisfy; picking this value is exactly the harness-calibration latitude v3Note already granted for this key, and W58 is stated as the phase's own second and final re-bless, so a hash-moving calendar-cadence change belongs here rather than a third re-bless inside W59. `seasons.yieldMilli` and `seasons.movementMilli` stay at identity [1000,1000,1000,1000] on purpose -- only the upkeep seam is built (W48/W49); yield and movement season terms do not exist in code and are explicitly out of this task's scope. The `upkeepMilli` array replacement itself was hand-edited after `publish.py`'s four other `set` operations landed: the tool's `set`/`--rename-key`/`--add-edge` primitives address a dict key or a selector-matched object inside an array, none of which can replace one element of a plain scalar array -- confirmed by reading `tools/tuning/publish.py` before hand-editing, not assumed.
